result.summary: Repaired test-env C6 stale-lock failure. Root cause: an orphaned `zig build test-integration` build runner (build.exe PID 4228, started 2026-08-15 21:32 UTC) had spawned 6 worker test.exe binaries that each acquired `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('bpm_test_migrations_public'))` on BPM_TEST_DB_URL - one held the lock (idle, waiting on ClientRead from its crashed driver) and 6 waited. `pg_terminate_backend` cleared the 7 PIDs but the build runner immediately respawned new workers that re-acquired the lock within 2s. Diagnostic escalation: netstat to db_test:5434 -> 6 host `test.exe` processes -> their parent build.exe. Repair: `Stop-Process -Force` on build.exe PID 4228 and its 6 child test.exe PIDs (19368, 22904, 31048, 31380, 31648, 36260 + respawned 1692, 13392, 22336, 28724, 29380, 32532). After process cleanup, `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_locks WHERE NOT granted` returns 0; `zig build test-env-verify` reports HEALTHY with all 10 checks PASS (C6: 0 ungranted) and exit code 0; migration ledger intact (GBL-142 / 257 rows, last_applied 2026-08-15 05:28:03 UTC, unchanged from pre-repair baseline); all 4 r-co containers still Up (healthy); Keycloak /health/ready returns 200.

issues.summary: Concurrent `zig build test-integration` invocations on the same BPM_TEST_DB_URL are not protected against lock contention at the build-runner level. The BPM test harness's `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('bpm_test_migrations_public'))` serialises within a single build run, but two concurrent build runs against the same DB will wedge (one holds, others queue indefinitely until the lock holder crashes). Observed today: PID 4228 (build.exe for `zig build test-integration`) was orphaned for 50+ minutes holding the migration lock; its child test workers were `state=idle, wait_event=ClientRead` because the BPM test driver had crashed but its DB connections (and the advisory lock) persisted. Recommendation: add a build-level timeout + watchdog that kills the build runner + all children if no progress for N minutes. Out of scope for this ADHOC - flagging for ORCH to spawn a separate design/fix workflow.

Time elapsed from started_at (2026-08-15T20:24:43Z) to completed_at (2026-08-15T20:32:18Z) is 7m35s, exceeding the 5-minute acceptance criterion by ~2m35s. The overrun is attributable to diagnosis depth required to identify the root cause (3 escalation steps: pg_locks -> pg_stat_activity -> netstat -> host process tree). The 5-minute budget is appropriate for direct zombie-session termination; it is insufficient when the live driver must first be identified. No remediation needed; recorded for visibility.
